coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2)
record.summary: A six-story board-formed concrete warehouse of 1941-44 (256 ft by 77 ft, 98,804 sq ft) north of Building 12, one of the three historic buildings Brookfield must rehabilitate to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards under the Pier 70 DDA. It is a Phase 1 option parcel to be held on a 99-year lease at an appraised rent; a 2021 filing described about 120 apartments in its shell, Brookfield now markets it as creative office, and the Port's proposed 2026 amendments would have the developer assign its option and close escrow within six months of Board approval, with certain impact fees and special taxes waived. No rehabilitation has started.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- RELOCATED 2026-09-16 from an incorrect west-lot placement (see digitization_method) to Figure 6.4.2's own labeled '2' Historic Building box, in the same east-side node as Buildings 12 and 21. Programmatically traced from this legend color, not hand-verified vertex-by-vertex; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, consistent with this site's other diagram-traced parcels. The close match (85%) between this trace's area and Warehouse No. 2's documented 236ft x 76ft footprint is a good independent sanity check, but this is still a simplified rectangle, not a surveyed building outline.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Officially 'Warehouse No. 2' per the D4D (Section 6.6.1), a historic industrial shop structure, footprint 236 ft x 76 ft. Brookfield's own leasing brochure lists its use as 'Office' (creative office), ~100,000 RSF of leasable space -- roughly double a sometimes-cited '~50,000 GSF, Arts/Maker' description, which understates both its size and its actual designated use. No source found confirms whether rehabilitation has started; absent from the Port's own June 2025 progress update.

Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation (D4D S6.6.1)
99 years (option parcel), rent by appraisal accounting for historic rehabilitation costs and tax credits
Phase 1 (Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan, Exhibit A)
Warehouse for the Building 12 complex and outfitting; commercial storage at the time of the nomination
Market Square is entered through 'an existing passageway through Buildings 2 and 12' and a 21st Street opening between Building 2 and Parcel D (D4D Section 3.9)

open_questions: No appraisal, lease, permit or construction record for Building 2 was found; the Port's June 2025 deck does not mention it and the 2026 report says no Phase 1 option has been exercised.

Which program is current: the 2021 filing's ~120 apartments or the leasing page's creative office. A June 2024 Chronicle piece reportedly describes the 2019 apartment plan as put on hold, but it could not be read (HTTP 403).
The RSF figure (~100,000) on Brookfield's brochure noted in the geometry file could not be verified; the NRHP gross area is 98,804 sq ft.
The 2026 memo's 'assign its option' language implies a third-party vertical developer for Building 2; none is named.
